annotation.title_en: Law Amending the Traffic Ordinance (No. 130), 5782-2022 (Autonomous Vehicles Pilot Regime)
annotation.venue: Sefer HaChukim (Israel Book of Laws) No. 2967
annotation.summary_en: Israeli statute amending the Traffic Ordinance to create a permit-based pilot regime for autonomous vehicles without drivers. It sets applicant conditions, remote control centers, cybersecurity, data retention, incident reporting, insurance, supervisory powers, and an advisory committee, with a National Traffic Supervisor issuing and suspending permits.
key_provisions_or_claims: Operating an autonomous driving system on roads requires a three-year operating permit from the National Traffic Supervisor, capped at 500 vehicles.
Permit holders must run a manned control center, minimal-risk-condition capability, and cyber-protection plans with SOC connection and 6-hour attack reporting.
Safety incidents must be reported within 24 hours; the Supervisor can order incident investigations, suspend permits, or halt operation.
Insurance is required; the Pool insurance route is limited to transitional periods and the Finance Minister may mandate third-party liability cover.
An advisory committee reviews technology, safety, privacy and the regime at least every three years.
